pr.title: Type a knob's value on the number row and glide it there, and quit field keys on Ctrl-C alone (instrument-knobs.md chunk 2)
pr.head: 78525efcd71599a2e2ee6060ec68f12072f4b3b5

summary: field keys plays the computer keyboard as a MIDI source named Field Keys. Chunk 1 of the instrument-knobs plan, #209 beneath this pull request, gave it knobs: a line of named knobs, each a MIDI controller (CC), that you choose with the left and right arrows and turn with up and down. Turning a knob across its whole range takes about 2.3 seconds of holding an arrow, and landing on a particular value means letting go in time.

This pull request is chunk 2: you can type the value instead. In musical, the default keymap, the number row types the chosen knob's value in the units its knob file names, so 800 on cutoff means 800 Hz. Enter completes the value. The knob then glides to the nearest of the controller's 128 values, sending one control change every 40 ms, at a speed set by the keymap's new glide field. Because the glide is a run of MIDI messages, a recorded take keeps it and any instrument answers it.

Two keys change meaning. Period (.), which bends the pitch up in musical, types the decimal point while a value is open, and bends otherwise. Esc cancels a value instead of quitting, and with no value open it puts Ctrl-C quits on the status line. Ctrl-C is now the only key that quits.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Knob. A named MIDI controller with a range, a curve, and units, read from a knob file such as juno.knobs.yaml.
  • Controller value. One of the 128 values, 0 to 127, that a MIDI control change carries. A knob maps each one to a value in its range.
  • Entry. The value you are typing, shown in the chosen knob's place until Enter, Esc, or a knob key closes it.
  • Glide. The run of control changes that moves a knob to a completed value, one per 40 ms tick at most.
  • Tick. One call of the session's tick(now), which a 40 ms timer makes while a turn key is held or a glide moves.
  • Position. A physical key, named as on a US keyboard (Digit1, Period), which is what a keymap binds.

cards.title: What this leaves for later
cards.html:
• Chunk 3, #212. A take that starts where your knobs are: .field/keys.json, the controllers passed in arm, and the daemon's chase. Criteria 20 and 21.
  • The criteria by hand. Criteria 4 to 8, 12, 14, 18, and 23 need a kitty terminal and ears. Plan §10.3 records them as owed, and the pull request body gives the steps.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• One open finding. The comment on the 40 ms timer in src/commands/keys.ts still says it runs only while a turn key is held, though it now runs during glides too (flagged on session.ts line 226).
  • Reviewed by reading. The commit's co-author trailer names the GitHub login claude, which has only read access, so the review ran none of the head's code. CI ran it instead.

groups.title: A keymap can type and set a glide speed
groups.kicker: The type action, the glide field, and musical's number row
intro: A keymap is a YAML file that maps each key position to a note or an action. This group adds one action and one field to its schema, and uses both in musical.

• { type: <c> } types one character into the chosen knob's value: a digit, written as a number from 0 to 9, or the string "-". The decimal point is not an action, because Period types it only while a value is open, in every keymap (see the session group).
  • glide is the seconds a typed value takes to cross a knob's whole range, so a shorter move takes its share. It defaults to 0, which sets a value at once, so a keymap that never mentions it types without a glide.
musical binds 1 to 0 and - to type, and sets glide: 1. tracker and fourths bind no type, so no value can open there and . keeps playing its note.

files.note: The type action, the glide field, and the reserved Escape's new message.

checks.text: type accepts only a whole number from 0 to 9 or the literal "-", and the schema test refuses ".", 10, "a", "1", and -1. Checked by reading the union and the test, which passes in CI on linux and windows.

files.note: The number row and - type, and glide: 1 crosses a knob's range in one second.

groups.title: Enter, Backspace, and Esc reach the session, and only Ctrl-C quits
groups.kicker: Key positions and the quit check
intro: field keys reads the keyboard through the kitty keyboard protocol, under which the terminal reports every key as an escape sequence, such as CSI 13 u for Enter. positionOf turns each key event into a position, and isQuit decides, before the session sees a key, whether that key ends the program.

Before this change, isQuit matched both Esc and Ctrl-C, and Enter and Backspace resolved to no position. Now positionOf names Enter, Escape, and Backspace, from codes 13, 27, and 127, and isQuit matches only Ctrl-C. The session decides what the three keys do.

No keymap can bind the three keys. Enter and Backspace are not bindable positions, and Escape stays reserved. A key pressed with Ctrl does nothing in a keymap either, so no keymap can stop Ctrl-C from quitting.

checks.text: A raw \x03 byte and CSI 99;5u still quit, and so does Ctrl at the US c position on a layout without a c, through the base layout key. A sequence cut off at the end of one read comes back as rest and is decoded with the next read, both while the daemon is still answering and in the play loop. Checked by reading decodeTerminal and both callers in src/commands/keys.ts.
Ctrl-D quit neither before this change nor after it. Under the protocol it arrives as CSI 100;5u, which isQuit ignores and the session's modifier rule drops.
None of the three is in the schema's BINDABLE_POSITIONS, so a keymap that names Enter or Backspace fails with the error for an unknown position, and one that names Escape with its reserved message.

groups.title: The session types, completes, and glides a value
groups.kicker: The entry, Period's two meanings, and a glide per controller
intro: KeysSession in src/keys/session.ts is the keyboard's state: it turns each press and release into MIDI messages and holds what the screen shows. Tests drive it without a terminal, and a 40 ms timer calls its tick(now) to move anything that changes over time.

An entry is the value being typed. The first type key opens one on the chosen knob. It holds digits, at most one ., and a - only as its first character, and a key that would break that does nothing. Every key not in the table below acts as usual, so notes keep playing while you type.

KeyWith an entry openWith none open
EnterCompletes itNothing
BackspaceDeletes the last character, and closes an empty entryNothing
EscCancels itShows Ctrl-C quits
PeriodTypes .The keymap's action, the bend up in musical
Left, rightCompletes it, then moves the choiceMoves the choice
Up, downCompletes it, then turns, which stops the glide it startedTurns

Completing an entry clamps the number to the knob's range and takes the controller value whose mapped value is nearest. With glide: 0 the session sends it at once. Otherwise it starts a glide: a record, kept per controller, of where the knob started, where it is going, and when. Each tick moves it by the time elapsed, so a late tick catches up, and sends at most one control change per controller. A turn of the gliding knob, a panic, a keymap reload, and quitting each stop it.

files.note: The entry, type(), complete(), the glides in tick(), and the keys handled before the keymap.

checks.text: Open finding. ticking() is now true while a glide moves, but the comment above the timer in src/commands/keys.ts line 283 still says the timer runs only while a turn key is held, and the function is still named tickWhileTurning. Reword the comment and rename the function.

Period with an entry open types . before the keymap is consulted and records nothing in held or heldControls, so its release sends nothing. A bend that Period began is in heldControls, so it ends on the release even if an entry opened while the key was held. Checked by tracing press and release. The session tests cover both cases.

With glide: 1 a glide moves 0.127 controller values a millisecond, so 127 to 62, 65 values, lands on the 13th 40 ms tick: 520 ms gives 66, capped at 65. Checked by hand and by the session test, which passes in CI.

Up or down completes the entry and then turns, and the turn deletes the glide that the completion just started. With glide above 0, the typed value is never sent, and the knob turns one step from where it was. Plan §2.7 step 5 asks for exactly this.
entry.label is written in type() but read only by a test. The knob line and complete() both use the chosen knob.

files.note: nearestController clamps a typed number and finds the nearest controller value.

checks.text: 800 on cutoff, 50 to 15000 Hz on the exp curve, lands on 62, which maps to 809.6 Hz, against 774.0 Hz for 61. 0.8 on attack, 0.005 to 4 s, lands on 96, which maps to 0.7824 s and prints 782 ms, against 0.8247 s for 97. Checked by computing the curve separately.

groups.title: The knob line shows the entry, and --print lists the typing keys
intro: The knob line sits between the instrument's line and the status line. It prints each knob's name and value at a fixed width, so turning a knob never moves the knobs after it or the notes on the status line.

While an entry is open, the chosen knob shows what you have typed, then _, then the units, padded to the value's width: cutoff 800_ Hz. An entry wider than the value widens that knob until the entry closes. The status line shows Ctrl-C quits through the session's existing message. field keys --print draws each typing key as its character on the number row and describes it as typing into the chosen knob's value.

files.note: KnobLine.text puts the entry in the chosen knob's place.

checks.text: The entry shows on the chosen knob, which is the knob complete() acts on. A knob key completes the entry before it moves the choice, and a knob file reload keeps the choice on the same name or closes the entry. Checked by reading control and setKnobs.

files.note: Tags a type key with its character, and describes it.

groups.title: The guide and the plans
groups.kicker: How to type a value, the one quit key, and what chunk 2 settled
intro: docs/keys.md is the user guide for field keys. It gains a "Type a value" section, the type action and the glide field in its keymap reference, and Ctrl-C as the one way to quit.

The instrument-knobs plan gains §10, which records what this chunk settled, what was verified and how, and what is still owed. keyboard-instrument.md §2.4 gets a dated note, because its rule was that Escape always quits.

files.note: The "Type a value" section, the type action and glide field, and Ctrl-C as the quit key.
